A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GASP, with matching authors, core components, and original experiments. All 28 pages of v1 and 38 pages of v2, including Appendices A–G, support comparison. Relocated material and reformatted figures and tables can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F report original attack-success, computational-efficiency, ablation, acquisition-function, and model-based and human readability results.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, benchmark evaluations, defended-model tests, Claude results, and component and sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The SuffixLLM–LBO–GASPEval–ORPO framework is retained. V2 corrects the specified ranking direction: v1 Algorithm 2 sorts GASPEval scores descending, whereas v2 Algorithms 2–3 sort ascending, consistent with lower scores indicating more harmful responses. Most expanded encoder, decoder, and search descriptions supply previously missing implementation details.

E1.justification: V2 adds direct AdvBench and HarmBench benchmark evaluations beyond the generated 100-prompt test set; AdvBench previously supplied training material. It also introduces scenarios with five explicit defenses protecting Mistral and Falcon, substantially extending the tested input environments (Table 3 and Figure 3(b)).

E2.justification: V1 evaluates GCG, AutoDAN, and AdvPrompter as attack baselines. V2 Table 2 adds PAIR, TAP, and ICA, materially broadening comparison with black-box methods. PAIR and TAP also enter the efficiency and automated-readability comparisons in Figure 2.

E3.justification: The original 75/25 training split and ASR@1/ASR@10 metrics remain. New experiments introduce four Claude configurations, five defense configurations on two target models, evaluator and fine-tuning controls, and representation-layer, query-budget, and initialization sweeps (Section 4 and Appendix F). These substantially expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained alignment ablation and acquisition-function study, v2 compares StrongREJECT versus GASPEval guidance and SFT versus ORPO. It adds layer-selection, query-budget, and initial-point sensitivity studies, explicit defense robustness tests, and an ICA failure example (Figures 3–4, 8, 10, and 12).

E5.justification: V1 does not specify repeated-run aggregation. V2 Appendix F.1 newly states that results are medians of three experimental runs. This is additional statistical reporting, without establishing an increase in runs for retained experiments. Neither version supplies empirical confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 retains the original Table 2 scores but adds extensive comparison, benchmark, Claude, defense, and ablation results. New findings are mixed: HarmBench/Mistral ASR@10 is 72% for GASP versus 76% for AdvPrompter (Table 3). The separate GPT Keyword Matching and StrongREJECT results from v1 Table 3 disappear, while its GASPEval results remain.

T1.justification: The readability-constrained attack objective remains. V2 replaces the generic distribution-approximation equation with an explicit SFT objective and formalizes ORPO, decoding, and the finite-candidate GASPEval surrogate. Appendix D also adds a claimed u + O(log M) query count without a proof. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central black-box, readability, efficiency, and adaptability claims remain. V2's contribution list newly asserts that GASP is the first framework to explore the embedding space for LLM jailbreaking. This introduces an explicit priority claim absent from v1.

C2.justification: V1 describes GP posterior convergence toward TargetLLM's response distribution; v2 instead develops a score-surrogate interpretation grounded in GASPEval. V2 also adds substantive interpretations of defended-model performance, deeper-layer representations, and query-budget tradeoffs, and acknowledges uncertainty about optimal ASR and opportunities to reduce query complexity (Sections 3–5 and Appendix F).

D1.justification: V2 provides substantially fuller training, search, and inference pseudocode, encoding and decoding details, candidate counts, and dataset-generation instructions. Appendix F adds Azure deployment, target-model sampling settings, and survey-participation details. The code-repository pointer changes. Most existing hyperparameters remain, but the maximum-suffix-length entry of 25 is omitted.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly relates its generator to AdvPrompter and adversarial training, expands positioning against black-box attacks, and develops the defense discussion. Added references include TAP, HarmBench, COLD-Attack, Self-Reminder, AutoDefense, and SafeDecoding. Several earlier embedding and optimization references, including t-SNE, are removed. These are substantive positioning changes.

P1.justification: The introduction and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Section 3 gains a separate ORPO subsection, readability moves into the main-results narrative, and generalization receives its own subsection. Appendix A is reorganized, the workflow discussion is condensed around expanded pseudocode, and the conclusion develops future directions.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with extensive regrouping and redrawing of displays. V1's alignment table becomes v2 Figure 4(a), GPT results become Figure 3(a), the survey plot moves to the appendix, and automated readability moves into the main text. New benchmark, defense, ablation, and sensitivity displays are added.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses an important validation gap by comparing GASP with black-box attack baselines and testing beyond its generated test set. Component-specific ablations and substantially clearer implementation descriptions improve scientific assessability and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the lost multi-evaluator GPT detail and a new cost-reporting inconsistency: Section 4.2 claims $5 total, whereas Table 5's listed costs sum to $11.08.
